relevance_note: Reports four HA20 patients in two Japanese families with TNFAIP3 variants: "We identified c.1434C>A:p.(Cys478*) in one family and a 236 kb deletion at 6q23.3 containing TNFAIP3 in another family."
method_note: Read the whole paper and built the JSON with a hand-written Python script in my scratch directory; every value was typed from my own reading (no automated table transcription). A resolver replaced only plain spaces/apostrophes with the paper's own characters (the paper uses thin spaces U+2009 before units, e.g. '39 °C', '1–2 weeks'), and every span was then checked verbatim against the paper by script. Table 1 has patients as columns; header row '| Patient | Patient 1 | Patient 2 | Patient 3 | Patient 4 |'; table spans quote from the row label through the patient's cell. Merged cells were NOT repeated in this conversion: the 'Family' and 'Detected variant' rows of Table 1 have empty cells for Patient 2 and Patient 4, so family and variant for those two come from the text (Sanger confirmation in patient 2; CNV in patients 3 and 4). Table 1 uses '+' and '–' (en dash) as present/absent markers, and the text corroborates '–' as absence (Patient 1 and Patient 4 ophthalmic/musculoskeletal/neurological negatives); I therefore recorded '–' cells as excluded, which departs from a literal reading of rule 6 ('-' = not reported) and should be reviewed. Broader absences were used to exclude narrower checklist items (no musculoskeletal signs/symptoms -> arthritis or arthralgia excluded; no ophthalmological symptoms -> uveitis excluded; no neurological symptoms -> CNS involvement excluded). Contradictions: (1) Patient 4: Table 1 'Fever' is '–' but the text says 'She presented fever with tonsillitis and lymphadenitis several times a year since her childhood' (not periodic); both phenotypic rows emitted and checklist 'recurrent fever' set to not reported. (2) Patient 2: Table 1 lists 'Oral ulcer, genital ulcer' as initial symptoms with onset 12 years, but the text says oral and genital ulcers began at 12 and 15 years respectively. (3) Patient 1: Table 1 marks 'Genital ulcers' '+' while the text names 'recurrent oral and perianal ulcers'; both genital and perianal ulcers recorded as observed. Other notes: Patient 3's normal colonoscopy (around 4-5 years) preceded endoscopic ulcers at 10 years, so it is recorded as a dated negative, not a contradiction; Patient 3 doses are recorded as printed ('colchicine (400 mg/day), cimetidine (1.0 mg/day)'); Table 1 lists PSL and NSAIDs for Patient 3 that the text does not mention; Patient 3 bloody-stool onset left null because '(at 5 years old)' follows 'weight loss'. The family 2 deletion also includes PERP; recorded once with gene TNFAIP3. Zygosity of the deletion recorded as heterozygous from 'TNFAIP3 haploinsufficiency'; its inheritance left not reported (paper only states qPCR confirmed it in the proband and her mother; father's result not given). Family 1 relatives are labelled 'III-1 in Fig. 1a' etc. because Fig. 1b reuses III-1 (Patient 3) and II-2 (Patient 4). Included one previously published individual described in the text (the 13 Mb 6q23.2-q24.3 deletion patient, ref [8]). Not given rows: Patient 3's father (WES performed, no label or result), 'other selected family members', DECIPHER/DGV/ExAC individuals (aggregate only), the 50 previously reported HA20 cases pooled in Table 2 (aggregate only), and the 10 families without TNFAIP3 variants. n_patients_reported = 4 first-hand patients (Table 2 pools 54). 'No BD-like symptoms' (II-6, I-1, I-2, II-3, II-4) was not used to exclude specific checklist items because the paper does not define it. II-5's amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is recorded as a feature but CNS involvement left not reported (not stated as such). Patient 2's erythema nodosum biopsy 'similar ... to cutaneous periarteritis nodosa' was not recorded as vasculitis. II-5's ALS diagnosis is not used as disease_label_as_stated.
